title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is studying a group M^{!~}_{0,3}[o] of 'rigidified' automorphisms u = u_{ξ,η} of the profinite group \hat Π_{0,3}. This is the Longue Marche setting of P^1 minus {0,1,∞} with its S_3 symmetry, whose orbifold quotient has π_1 equal to PSL_2(Z). An automorphism u is determined by where it sends two generators: u(σ_∞) = η σ_∞ and u(ρ) = ξ ρ (formula 163). The parameters (ξ,η) satisfy the 'équation des lacets'. One composes with the natural map \hat Π_{0,3} → SL(2,\hat Z), defined up to ±1, written x ↦ \underline x.

What the previous page did. It linearised the condition u(ε_0) = ε_0^μ inside GL(2,\hat Z), with ε_0 = (1 −1; 0 1).
- This forces N = 0 and L = μP.
- The determinant normalisation det = μ then forces P^2 = 1.
- With P = 1 one gets \underline u_ξ = (μ M; 0 1), an element of the upper Borel subgroup B.

Top of this page. The image \underline ξ = (A B; C D) satisfies AD − BC = 1, C + DB = 1 and D ∈ \hat Z^*. It is expressed through the Borel entries by D = 1/μ and B = M/μ. Hence C = 1 − M/μ^2 and A is determined. So ξ and \underline u_ξ determine each other (163 bis).

Theorem (165). The map u_{ξ,η} ↦ \underline u_ξ, from M^{!~}_{0,3}[o] to GL(2,\hat Z)' (taken mod ±1), is a group homomorphism.
- A first marginal NB says that on M^{!~}_{0,3}(o) one even gets a homomorphism to GL(2,\hat Z) itself, not only modulo ±1.
- A second NB says the map factors through the Borel group B of (169).

Proof.
- Step (166), equivariance: \underline{u(x)} = \underline u · \underline x · \underline u^{-1}. It suffices to check this on the generators σ_∞ and ρ, where it is (161)/(163).
- Step (167): the composition law of the group (139) is ξ'' = u'(ξ)·ξ'. Applying the reduction and (166) gives \underline ξ'' = int(\underline u_{ξ'})(\underline ξ) · \underline ξ'.
- What remains is to show that three matrix solutions linked by (167) satisfy \underline u_{ξ''} = \underline u_{ξ'} · \underline u_ξ (168).

Next page. The problem is recast as a 1-cocycle identity for F_ξ : B → SL(2,\hat Z), essentially \underline u ↦ [\underline u, ρ] = \underline u ρ \underline u^{-1} ρ^{-1} up to a determinant factor. This is trivially a cocycle, since u ↦ int(u)(ρ)ρ^{-1} always is.

Corollary (172). Extending by the S_3 part gives a homomorphism M^{!~}_{0,3} → GL(2,\hat Z)'.

In modern terms: this is the 'linearisation', or congruence-quotient shadow, of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group. Its image is the Borel subgroup {(μ M; 0 1)}. Here μ plays the role of the cyclotomic-type parameter λ, and M is a second, additive (unipotent) invariant.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this page. The proof is reduced, correctly, to a cocycle identity that is completed on the next page.

Minor gap: the choice P = 1 among the solutions of P^2 = 1 is only called 'the most evident'. The sign ambiguity is absorbed by working mod ±1 (GL(2,\hat Z)'), but over \hat Z the equation P^2 = 1 has more solutions than ±1 (for example at the prime 2 and via CRT idempotent combinations). The margin note claiming a lift to GL(2,\hat Z) on M(o) is therefore not fully justified here.
The determinant factor in F_ξ on the next page is handled loosely; it is irrelevant modulo scalars ±1 and det of a commutator is 1, but the bookkeeping is not explicit.

ideas.what: Equivariance of the reduction map \hat Π_{0,3} → SL(2,\hat Z) with respect to the automorphisms u, i.e. \underline{u(x)} = \underline u · \underline x · \underline u^{-1}.
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT-type automorphisms on the congruence completion of PSL_2(Z) / Γ(2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Later GT literature on actions on \widehat{SL_2(Z)} and congruence quotients (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Boggi et al.)
ideas.where_published: Spirit of the Esquisse d'un programme and the Longue Marche (PSL_2(Z) and S_3-symmetry of M_{0,4}); this explicit formula: unsure

ideas.what: Homomorphism from the rigidified automorphism group M^{!~}_{0,3}[o] onto the Borel subgroup {(μ M; 0 1)} of GL(2,\hat Z) mod ±1. This yields an invariant M beyond the cyclotomic-type parameter μ.
ideas.modern_name: Linearised / congruence image of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (λ together with an additional unipotent parameter)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT, 1990); Ihara; Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura (actions on the profinite SL_2(Z))

ideas.what: Reduction of the homomorphism property to the 1-cocycle identity F(u'u) = int(u')(F(u)) · F(u') for u ↦ [u,ρ].
ideas.modern_name: Coboundary-type (inner) 1-cocycle; the composition law of GT expressed as a cocycle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; the GT composition law f'' = f'(f)·f is due to Drinfeld (1990)
ideas.where_published: The composition law (139) appears in the Longue Marche / these notes

missed.claim: Grothendieck computes the image of his GT-type group in the congruence completion GL(2,\hat Z)/±1. He finds it lies in the Borel {(μ M; 0 1)}, with ξ and \underline u determining each other. This gives an explicit pre-Drinfeld 'linear shadow' of GT carrying, besides μ (∼λ), an additive parameter M, compatible with the S_3 extension (Corollary 172). Later work on the GT action on congruence quotients of \widehat{SL_2(Z)} reaches similar conclusions, but this explicit early formulation is not in the record.
missed.quote: Théorème L'application (165) M_{0,3}^{!~}[o] → Gl(2,\hat Z) ... u_{ξ,η} ↦ \underline u_ξ ... est un homom. de groupes.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is historical priority evidence that Grothendieck studied the congruence/linear quotient of his GT-type group in the 1980s. The parameter M could be compared with known invariants of GT and G_Q on the congruence quotient, but this is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine but genuinely GT-flavoured computation: the homomorphism of a pre-Drinfeld GT-like group to a Borel subgroup of GL(2,\hat Z). The proof itself is a trivial cocycle check, and the result is unsurprising to specialists, who know the congruence quotient sees little beyond the cyclotomic character. Its interest is mainly historical.
transcription_corrections: Target group in (165): the decoration after Gl(2,\hat Z) is most likely a prime, Gl(2,\hat Z)' (reduction mod ±1, as used on the next page), rather than '#'.
First margin NB: likely reads 'NB Du fait qu'on peut se restreindre à M_{0,3}^{!~}(o), on trouve un homom. dans Gl(2,\hat Z), pas seulement dans Gl(2,\hat Z)/±1' (the transcription garbles this).
Second margin NB: likely 'NB cette application se factorise par le groupe B ci-dessous (169)'.
In the proof, the reference after 'où cette formule est évidente' is (161) in the image, which refers to formulas around (163).
